title: Chemical Oxygen Generator — Displacement Check and Retention Inspection in the Passenger Service Unit
abstract: Displacement check of the chemical oxygen generator in its cradle and inspection of the retention arrangement, with the handling precautions that apply to a live generator and the strap tension check.

sections.purpose: This task gives the displacement check of the chemical oxygen generator in its cradle, the inspection of the retention arrangement and the strap tension check, for the scheduled cabin inspection and after any service unit disturbance.
sections.job_setup_note: The generator is live. It fires if the lanyard is pulled and the reaction cannot be stopped once started, so the firing loop must be disconnected before the strap is released and the lanyard must be secured throughout. The service unit is dropped on its hinge and must be supported; the hinge is not designed to carry the unit at full travel with a person working on it. Use the handling cradle whenever a generator is out of its mounting.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm from the cabin log that the oxygen system is not armed. 2. Drop the passenger service unit on its hinge and support it on the prop. WARNING: DO NOT PULL OR SNAG THE FIRING LANYARD. THE GENERATOR FIRES ON LANYARD PULL AND REACHES 260 DEGREES CELSIUS WITHIN SECONDS. 3. Disconnect the firing loop at the connector and cap it. 4. Measure the displacement of the generator forward face from the cradle datum with the depth gauge. 5. Record the measurement. A generator beyond the displacement limit must be reseated and the retention arrangement replaced. 6. Examine the retaining strap for relaxation, fraying and correct routing. 7. Confirm that the secondary retention bracket is fitted at the aft end of the cradle and that its two screws are secure. 8. Do the strap tension check with the calibrated torque wrench and re-tension to the value in the figure if it is low. 9. Examine the cradle for cracking at the mounting feet. 10. Reconnect the firing loop and do the continuity check. 11. Raise the service unit and latch it, then confirm the latch is fully home.
sections.close_out: Confirm that every service unit worked has been latched and that no panel is left unsecured. Record the displacement measurement for each generator position, whether the retention bracket was found fitted and any generator reseated, in the cabin maintenance record. Report any generator found beyond the displacement limit.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Step 7 applies only to aircraft post MOD-146830.

safety_precautions: Confirm that the oxygen system is not armed.
Do not pull or snag the firing lanyard.
Support the passenger service unit on the prop before you work on it.

title: Chemical Oxygen Generator — Displacement Check and Retention Inspection in the Passenger Service Unit

issue.reason: Retention step rewritten to check the end cap type rather than the presence of the bracket, with a caution on the combination that gives no retention.

abstract: Displacement check of the chemical oxygen generator in its cradle and inspection of the retention arrangement, including the end cap type that the secondary retention depends on, with the handling precautions for a live generator and the strap tension check.

sections.purpose: This task gives the displacement check of the chemical oxygen generator in its cradle, the inspection of the retention arrangement and the strap tension check, for the scheduled cabin inspection and after any service unit disturbance.
sections.job_setup_note: The generator is live. It fires if the lanyard is pulled and the reaction cannot be stopped once started, so the firing loop must be disconnected before the strap is released and the lanyard must be secured throughout. The secondary retention works only as a pair: the bracket at the aft end of the cradle and the machined end cap that engages it. A bracket found with the original moulded cap is the combination this task exists to detect, and it looks correct from the aisle. The service unit is dropped on its hinge and must be supported; the hinge is not designed to carry the unit at full travel with a person working on it. Use the handling cradle whenever a generator is out of its mounting.
sections.procedure: 1. Confirm from the cabin log that the oxygen system is not armed. 2. Drop the passenger service unit on its hinge and support it on the prop. WARNING: DO NOT PULL OR SNAG THE FIRING LANYARD. THE GENERATOR FIRES ON LANYARD PULL AND REACHES 260 DEGREES CELSIUS WITHIN SECONDS. 3. Disconnect the firing loop at the connector and cap it. 4. Measure the displacement of the generator forward face from the cradle datum with the depth gauge. 5. Record the measurement. A generator beyond the displacement limit must be reseated and the retention arrangement replaced. 6. Examine the retaining strap for relaxation, fraying and correct routing. 7. Where the retention bracket is fitted, confirm that the end cap recess engages the bracket. CAUTION: A BRACKET FITTED WITH THE ORIGINAL END CAP GIVES NO RETENTION. CHECK THE END CAP TYPE, NOT ONLY THE PRESENCE OF THE BRACKET. 8. Do the strap tension check with the calibrated torque wrench and re-tension to the value in the figure if it is low. 9. Examine the cradle for cracking at the mounting feet. 10. Reconnect the firing loop and do the continuity check. 11. Raise the service unit and latch it, then confirm the latch is fully home.
sections.close_out: Confirm that every service unit worked has been latched and that no panel is left unsecured. Record the displacement measurement for each generator position, the retention standard found and any generator reseated, in the cabin maintenance record. Report any generator found beyond the displacement limit.

type_data.effectivity_note: All aircraft. Step 7 applies only to aircraft post MOD-146830, and on those aircraft the end cap type is what is being checked; the presence of the bracket alone is not an acceptable finding.

safety_precautions: Confirm that the oxygen system is not armed.
Do not pull or snag the firing lanyard.
Support the passenger service unit on the prop before you work on it.
